metaDescription: Six inverter chargers for 50 amp RV service compared on dual-leg transfer switches, charger current, battery chemistry and honest surge ratings.
expertTake: The Go Power Advanced 3000W with a dual-leg 50A transfer switch is the best pick because it is the only unit here built for 50 amp shore power as a whole. The ECO-WORTHY 1000W is the value pick for a small coach. Anyone with a 30 amp RV can skip the dual-leg hardware and choose a simpler single-leg unit.
introParagraphs: A large coach is wired differently from a small one. Its shore cord carries two hot legs rather than one, and a transfer switch that serves only one of them leaves half the coach dead whenever the inverter takes over.

An inverter charger folds three jobs into one box: it makes AC from the battery, charges the battery from shore power and switches the load between them. The right choice depends on how many legs the switch passes, how fast the charger refills a bank, and which battery chemistry you run.

products.name: Go Power Advanced 3000W inverter charger, dual-leg 50A transfer switch
products.description:
Dual-leg 50A is the phrase that matters for this unit. It combines a 3000W sine wave inverter, a battery charger and a shore-power transfer switch rated for two legs of fifty amps, which is exactly what a 50 amp coach needs. Without that, an inverter can only back up one leg and half the coach loses power when shore power drops.

The design is high-frequency, compact and lightweight, which makes installation easier than with the old heavy transformer units. For a coach with a big bank and a plan to boondock, a single box that handles shore power, charging and inverting reduces wiring. It also simplifies the question of how to keep the inverter from back-feeding the pedestal, since the transfer switch is built in.

It sits near the top of the price tiers, and the listing gives few details on charger current, so confirm that figure before buying. A 3000W inverter at 12V draws about 280A at full load, so cable and bank sizing apply. Mount it in a ventilated bay and follow the manual's wiring diagram exactly. For an owner with a true 50 amp coach, this is the logical centerpiece.
products.bestFor: Owners of 50 amp coaches who want one unit that handles both legs.
pros: Dual-leg 50A transfer switch fits 50 amp service
Inverter, charger and switch in one box
High-frequency design is compact and light
3000W sine wave output
cons: Near the top of the price tiers
Charger current is not stated in the listing

products.name: Xantrex Freedom XC Pro 3000 inverter charger, 150A
products.description:
A 150A battery charger is the number that stands out on the Xantrex Freedom XC Pro 3000. That current refills a large lithium bank quickly when shore power or a generator is available, which matters because a 400Ah bank would otherwise take a day to recover. The unit is described as an all-in-one true sine wave inverter with a built-in lithium-ion capable charger.

Its power boost doubles the continuous output for five seconds or more, helping with motor loads such as a compressor start. A 3000W inverter with that boost can handle a microwave and a coffee maker with room to spare. Xantrex is an established name in RV power gear, which counts for support and parts.

It sits at an upper-middle tier. The listing does not mention a dual-leg transfer switch, so a 50 amp coach needs an external one or must use only one leg for the inverter circuits. Confirm the switch rating before you buy. For a coach with a lithium bank and a plan to run heavy loads, the 150A charger is the best feature in the group.
products.bestFor: Owners with a large lithium bank who want fast shore-power or generator charging.
pros: 150A charger refills a big bank quickly
True sine output at 3000W
Power boost doubles output for five seconds
Established RV power brand
cons: Listing does not mention a dual-leg switch
Full inverter load still draws about 280A

products.name: Go Power GP-IC3000-12 inverter charger, 125A, 4800W surge
products.description:
Ratings are spelled out here in a way few listings manage: 4800W for five seconds and 6000W for one second of surge, above 90 percent efficiency and a 125A power-factor-corrected charger. Those figures let you judge a motor start, a battery refill time and a heat load. The companion listing for the same model describes a 100A automatic transfer switch, which is 50A per leg.

A 50A-per-leg transfer switch is what a 50 amp coach needs, and it is the point where this model matches the Advanced unit above. It is an older platform with a heavier transformer-based feel and built-in handles for installation, which is helpful when you are lifting a heavy box into a bay.

It sits at the middle of the price tiers, below the newer high-frequency design. The extra weight is the tradeoff. Verify the exact model number before you buy, since similar listings exist. A 3000W inverter at 12V draws about 280A, so use heavy cable and a proper fuse. For a coach that needs a proven, documented unit, this is a safe choice.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a proven, fully documented 3000W unit with a 50A-per-leg switch.

125A power-factor-corrected charger
Efficiency stated above 90 percent
100A transfer switch, 50A per leg
cons: Middle price tier on an older platform

products.name: Victron MultiPlus-II 3000VA 12V inverter charger, 2x120V, 120A
products.description:
Power Assist is the Victron's distinctive feature. When shore power or a generator is limited, the inverter adds battery power to the incoming supply so a small source can feed a larger load without tripping. In a campground with a weak pedestal or a small generator, that is a real advantage. It also provides power without interruption when shore or generator power drops.

The MultiPlus-II offers two 120V outputs and a 120A charger, and up to six units can run in parallel for far more capacity. The two outputs suit the two-leg layout of a 50 amp coach. Victron is the choice of many serious installers because of its monitoring, configurability and parts availability.

It sits at the top of the price tiers, and it asks for more installation skill: it is configured through software and needs a proper system design. If you want a plug-and-play box, choose a Go Power unit. If you are building an expandable system and want the best monitoring, this is the premier option. Plan the cable and fuse sizing carefully.
products.bestFor: Serious installers who want Power Assist, two outputs and expandable capacity.

120A charger

Full inverter load still draws about 280A

products.name: VEVOR 2000W inverter charger, 5 working modes, LCD remote

specList.label: Working modes
specList.value: Five, including grid and battery priority

products.description:
Five working modes are what VEVOR offers beyond the basics. The listing names an unattended mode, grid priority and battery priority among them, which lets you decide whether the coach runs on shore power with the inverter as a backup or on the battery first. That control matters for solar owners who want to use the sun before the grid.

The 2000W pure sine output covers a microwave, a coffee maker and a laptop, and an LCD with a remote makes it easy to monitor. It is designed for 12V battery systems and is compatible with a variety of battery types. It is sized for a smaller coach than the 3000W units.

The listing does not describe a dual-leg transfer switch, so it suits a 30 amp coach or a single-leg circuit better than a full 50 amp installation. It sits at the lower-middle tier, which is attractive for the feature set. Verify the charger current and the transfer rating in the manual. For a small coach with solar, it is a flexible and affordable choice.
products.bestFor: Small-coach and solar owners who want selectable working modes at a fair price.
pros: Five working modes including grid and battery priority
2000W pure sine with LCD and remote
Designed for 12V battery systems
Lower-middle price tier
cons: No dual-leg transfer switch is described
Charger details need checking in the manual

products.name: ECO-WORTHY 1000W inverter charger, 55A LiFePO4 charger, 20ms UPS
products.description:
A 20 millisecond switchover is the feature that turns this ECO-WORTHY into a quiet UPS for the coach. When shore power drops, the unit moves to battery power within 20ms, which is fast enough that most electronics do not notice. It combines a 1000W pure sine inverter with a 55A charger tuned for LiFePO4 batteries.

That pairing suits a small coach with a modest lithium bank. A 55A charger refills a 200Ah bank in roughly four hours from empty, depending on the state of charge. The 1000W inverter runs a TV, a laptop and a small microwave, though not a heavy kitchen load.

It sits at the lowest tier among the six, which makes it the value pick. It is not built for the dual 50A legs of a full 50 amp coach, so use it on a single circuit or in a smaller RV. The listing says nothing about a dual-leg switch. Check the transfer switch rating against your circuit before you connect it. For a van or a small trailer with lithium, it is a sensible, inexpensive solution.
products.bestFor: Van and small-trailer owners with a lithium bank who want a low-cost inverter charger.

20ms switchover acts like a UPS

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 50 amp coach has two 120V legs of fifty amps each. The Go Power Advanced 3000W lists a dual-leg 50A switch and the Go Power GP-IC3000-12 lists a 100A switch with 50A per leg. A single-leg switch leaves half the coach without power when shore power drops. Check this first.

The charger refills the bank from shore power or a generator. The Xantrex offers 150A, the Go Power GP-IC3000-12 125A, the Victron 120A and the ECO-WORTHY 55A. Charge time in hours is roughly bank amp-hours divided by charger amps. A 400Ah bank takes about three hours at 125A, in theory.

Lithium and lead acid charge differently. The Xantrex is lithium-ion capable, the ECO-WORTHY is tuned for LiFePO4 and the VEVOR works with many types. A charger profile that does not match the battery can shorten its life, so check the supported chemistries.

Surge covers motor starts for seconds. The Go Power GP-IC3000-12 states 4800W for 5 seconds and efficiency above 90 percent, and the Xantrex boosts 2x for five seconds. Units that give no figure leave you guessing about a compressor start.

A weak pedestal or a small generator can trip under a big load. The Victron's Power Assist adds battery power to help. Others simply switch to the battery. Decide whether you camp at weak parks or run a small generator.

The Go Power Advanced is high-frequency, compact and lightweight, while the GP-IC3000-12 is an older heavier design with built-in handles. The Victron needs configuration software. Match the box to your skill and your bay.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit to 50 amp service
howWeEvaluated.description: We gave the most weight to dual-leg transfer switches. The Go Power Advanced and the GP-IC3000-12 lead. Units without a stated dual-leg switch were treated as single-leg.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charger capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared charger current from 55A on the ECO-WORTHY to 150A on the Xantrex and noted chemistry compatibility. Faster chargers earn points for lithium banks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Documentation
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited stated surge, efficiency and switch ratings. The Go Power GP-IC3000-12 provides the most numbers. Sparse listings scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: System features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at Power Assist, working modes, UPS speed and parallel capability. The Victron and VEVOR lead on flexibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how easy each box is to install. The compact Go Power Advanced is the easiest, and the Victron needs the most setup.

cards.label: Dual-leg
cards.text: The Go Power Advanced and GP-IC3000-12 pass both legs of 50 amp service. The whole coach keeps power when the inverter takes over, which is what a 50 amp RV needs.

cards.label: Single-leg
cards.text: The ECO-WORTHY and VEVOR suit a 30 amp coach or one circuit. Half of a 50 amp coach stays unpowered unless you add a second switch or reduce the loads.

howToChoose.note: Choose dual-leg for a full 50 amp coach, single-leg for a smaller one.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A fast charger for generator time, low idle draw and a transfer switch that handles your service. A 125A charger refills about 125Ah per hour, so a generator running two hours restores a decent share of a bank.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Xantrex with 150A and the Victron with Power Assist suit boondockers with generators. The ECO-WORTHY suits smaller banks.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You own a true 50 amp coach, a large lithium bank or want expansion. The Go Power Advanced 3000W, Xantrex and Victron cover those needs.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your coach is small or runs a single circuit. The ECO-WORTHY 1000W and VEVOR 2000W provide inverting and charging at lower tiers.

faq.q: What does 50 amp RV service mean for an inverter?
faq.a: A 50 amp coach has two 120V legs of fifty amps each. The inverter charger's transfer switch must pass both legs, or half the coach loses power when the inverter takes over.

faq.q: Can I use a 30 amp inverter charger in a 50 amp RV?
faq.a: Only on a single circuit or with extra switching. A 30 amp unit cannot pass the full 50 amp load, so plan which circuits the inverter will serve.

faq.q: How fast will a charger refill my bank?
faq.a: Roughly bank amp-hours divided by charger amps. A 125A charger refills a 400Ah bank in about three hours in theory, longer in practice as the charge tapers.

faq.q: Do I need pure sine at 50 amps?
faq.a: Yes. Microwaves, TVs and refrigerators run better on it. All six units here state a pure or true sine output.

faq.q: Is lithium compatible with these chargers?
faq.a: The ECO-WORTHY is tuned for LiFePO4, the Xantrex is lithium-ion capable and the Victron is configurable. Check the manual for your battery.

faq.q: Can an inverter charger run my rooftop air conditioner?
faq.a: A 3000W unit with a power boost can start a small air conditioner, but a 12V bank would drain quickly. Most owners run air conditioning only on shore power or a generator.
